title: Work and business
description: Words for careers, employment, the workplace, companies and the economy in Writing Task 2 and Speaking Parts 1 and 3.

words.definition: the feeling of enjoying and being fulfilled by your work
words.example: For many young workers, job satisfaction matters more than a high salary.

words.definition: the balance between time spent working and time for personal life
words.example: Flexible hours can help parents achieve a better work-life balance.

words.definition: the state of not having a job, or the number of people without jobs
words.example: Youth unemployment remains a serious concern in many developing economies.

words.definition: a person who starts their own business, often taking financial risks
words.example: Social media has made it easier for young entrepreneurs to reach customers.

words.definition: working from home or another place outside the office
words.example: Remote working has reduced commuting time for millions of employees.

words.definition: a move to a higher position in a company
words.example: Staff who take training courses are more likely to be considered for promotion.

words.definition: all the people who work in a company, industry or country
words.example: Women now make up almost half of the country's workforce.

words.definition: having lost your job because your employer no longer needs you
words.example: Hundreds of factory workers were made redundant when the plant closed.

words.definition: a labour market of short-term or freelance jobs rather than permanent ones
words.example: Ride-hailing drivers are a well-known example of the gig economy.

words.definition: working for several clients rather than one employer
words.example: Many designers prefer freelance work because of the freedom it offers.

words.definition: something that encourages a person to do something
words.example: Bonuses are a common incentive to improve sales performance.

words.definition: the rate at which a person or company produces goods or work
words.example: Some studies suggest that shorter working weeks can actually increase productivity.

words.definition: to find new people to join a company or organisation
words.example: Technology firms struggle to recruit enough qualified engineers.

words.definition: a person you work with
words.example: Working from home can make it harder to build relationships with colleagues.

words.definition: the chances of being successful and advancing in a job
words.example: A second language can significantly improve your career prospects.

words.definition: to pay another company to do work rather than doing it yourself
words.example: Many firms outsource their customer service to other countries.

words.definition: a new, small company, often in technology
words.example: Jakarta has become one of Asia's fastest-growing hubs for tech start-ups.

words.definition: the money a company receives from selling goods or services
words.example: Online sales now account for over half of the company's revenue.

words.definition: making money
words.example: Small farms struggle to remain profitable when crop prices fall.

words.definition: the amount of work a person has to do
words.example: Teachers often complain about a heavy workload of marking and paperwork.

words.definition: the lowest amount of pay that employers are legally allowed to pay
words.example: Raising the minimum wage could reduce poverty but may also cost some jobs.

words.definition: abilities that are useful in many different jobs
words.example: Volunteering helps students develop transferable skills such as teamwork.

words.definition: a large company with offices or factories in many countries
words.example: Multinationals are often attracted to countries with low labour costs.

words.definition: a person who buys goods or services
words.example: Consumers are increasingly influenced by online reviews.

words.definition: the joining of two companies into one
words.example: The merger of the two airlines led to hundreds of job losses.

words.definition: a system where people work at different times of the day or night
words.example: Long-term shift work can disrupt sleep patterns and health.

words.definition: to travel regularly between home and work
words.example: Many employees commute more than two hours a day.

words.definition: to start producing or offering a wider range of goods or services
words.example: Coffee farmers are being encouraged to diversify into other crops.

words.definition: the rate at which employees leave a company and are replaced
words.example: Low pay is the main reason for high staff turnover in the hotel industry.

words.definition: a heavy responsibility or cost
words.example: High taxes can be a heavy burden on small businesses.
